answer: Each identity joins a crystal lattice by posting a bond that grows with the lattice size, so N clones cost roughly N squared in total. Every epoch a public pulse selects one random cell; the chosen identity must solve a cipher challenge salted with its own address and that pulse, a memory-hard sequential proof no farm can parallelize or outsource. One proven fake fractures the whole crystal: every bond in the lattice slashes at once, so a Sybil farm loses all N squared of its stake on a single detection while honest members keep earning.
